headline_marked: [[Google Play Store gets Gemini AI overhaul]] with 'Ask Play' for smarter app discovery
headline: Google Play Store gets Gemini AI overhaul with 'Ask Play' for smarter app discovery
summary: Google's new "Ask Play" feature, powered by Gemini, introduces interactive AI search and multi-step queries to help users find the perfect app without endless scrolling.
details: Google announced a major Gemini-powered overhaul to app discovery at its May 2026 I/O conference. The new "Ask Play" feature aims to make the Play Store better at understanding intent-based searches, moving beyond simple keyword matching.

Ask Play provides an interactive AI search overlay where users can describe their needs naturally. It handles multistep searches, remembering context to refine recommendations as criteria are narrowed down.
For example, users can ask for a puzzle game without a paywall, then immediately refine the search to "Now only show me the ones that play offline." This eliminates the need to restart searches.

Another new feature, Ask Play Highlights, offers high-level summaries directly in search results. This allows users to quickly gauge an app's suitability before clicking into its full listing, saving time.
Google is also introducing "Play Shorts," a vertical video feed of app gameplay and interfaces within the Play Store. This aims to engage users who are "window-shopping" for new apps.
For developers, this update means a shift towards clear, concise app descriptions that plainly explain value. Gemini's semantic understanding will prioritize apps that genuinely meet user intent.

The AI-driven discovery layer will also leverage reviews, ratings, and engagement metrics more effectively. For instance, an app with recent developer replies addressing sync issues might get an edge in searches for "best budgeting app that doesn't have bank sync problems."

Beyond the Play Store, Google is also launching Play Games Sidekick, an in-game AI assistant. Gamers can swipe in the overlay for tips and help when stuck, replacing the need to tab out to external guides.
The new system is expected to improve over time, despite potential initial rough edges. Developers are encouraged to audit their store listings to adapt to the AI-driven discovery funnel.

headline: Pest Architecture Tests caught a data leak a code review missed
summary: A five-line architecture test using Pest PHP successfully identified a multi-tenant data leak that had slipped past a human code review, preventing further exposure.
details: A developer added a new model and forgot a crucial BelongsToTenant trait, leading to a multi-tenant data leak where one clinic could see fragments of another's data. This critical oversight was missed by a human code reviewer focused on business logic.

Architecture tests, unlike traditional behavior tests, check the structure and organization of code rather than its computational output. They assert rules about how code should be designed, such as ensuring specific traits are used by certain models.

The missing trait allowed data from one tenant to be visible to another in a specific report for two days before a support ticket flagged the issue. Standard behavioral tests failed to detect this structural flaw.

These architecture tests are integrated into Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines, failing the build on every commit if a rule is broken. This immediately flags violations, naming the rule and the offending file.

Beyond the initial data leak, the tenant trait test identified four more models missing the trait in subsequent months, each representing a potential data breach. Other architecture tests can prevent issues like direct env calls outside config files or database queries in controllers.

For existing large codebases, a gradual rollout is crucial: start with one critical rule, fix its violations, and then add one new rule per week. This allows teams to absorb changes and fix issues without being overwhelmed.

Ignoring methods can be used to exclude legacy code from new rules, enforcing them only on new code while old code is refactored on its own schedule. Tracking these exceptions ensures new code doesn't fall into old patterns.

Architecture tests ensure codebase predictability and verifiable guarantees. When every tenant model provably uses the required trait, data isolation becomes a fact verified by the build, not just a hope.
